### Introduction
The Human Protein Atlas (HPA) is a research project which was initiated in 2003 with the aim of mapping all the human proteins in cells, tissues, and organs using various omics technologies.

Using HPA data, I am keen to calculate the total number of genes categorised as having regionally elevated expression in the forebrain - that is, the cerebral cortex, basal ganglia, thalamus and hypothalamus - regions in human, pig and mouse.


### Results

* Human: 180, 83, 57, 110
* Pig: 109, 157, 31, 45
* Mouse: 55, 185, 60, 98

```{r}
human_total <- sum(180, 83, 57, 110)
pig_total <- sum(109, 157, 31, 45)
mouse_total <- sum(55, 185, 60, 98)

print(paste("The total number for human is", human_total))
print(paste("The total number for pig is", pig_total))
print(paste("The total number for mouse is", mouse_total))
```

### Conclusion
The species [human]{.mark} had the highest number of genes with regionally elevated expression in the forebrain
